note: Most of these are solo fiddle: tunes are named after places, people or legends, with the dance type (springar, gangar, halling) in the title.

size.basis: No catalogue counts recordings. The repertoire is over 1000 registered slåttar for the Hardanger fiddle plus variants, 400 of them from Telemark (Norwegian Wikipedia, Hardingfele). Commercial output runs from 78s by the 1920s (Halvor Bråthen, 1928) through solo albums of 14-26 tunes each by players such as Knut Buen, Hauk Buen, the Bjørgums, Knut Hamre (12 albums), Benedicte Maurseth and Annbjørg Lien on Heilo, Grappa, Sylvartun and Etnisk Musikklubb, plus Ocora and archive series. Recordings of tunes on releases are estimated at a few thousand; archive tapes (Norsk folkemusikksamling) would add more. Core is what a player would call the essential tunes and performances across Telemark, Setesdal, Hardanger, Voss, Valdres and Hallingdal.
